newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Parliament limits TPS rights to public TV.
newsitem.headline: French Parliament limits TPS rights to public TV.

text.p: France's National Assembly has put a three-year time limit on an exclusive deal to carry public television channels France 2 and France 3 on Television par Satellite (TPS), a digital statellite TV station.

The move, part of a debate on a broadcasting bill covering the future of public channels, FM frequencies and digital television, comes after a long battle between TPS and pay TV firm Canal Plus, which wanted the two public channels on its Canalsatellite digital satellite service.

The National Assembly, France's upper house of Parliament, on Thursday also voted to ban pay television channels from buying exclusive rights to broadcast major sporting events, saying these must be freely available to all.
It also agreed to allow national channels to broadcast national advertising during breaks in regional programmes. Private channel M6 had lobbied for this.
TPS's exclusive rights to France 2 and France 3 were extended to three years in the debate, which began on Tuesday, from a two year limit originally suggested in the bill.
During the three years, broadcasters must develop a single decoder so that subscribers can subscribe to differerent services without having to change decoder.

However, Culture Minister Philippe Douste-Blazy said in an interview with daily newspaper La Tribune, published on Thursday, that the limit on TPS's exclusive rights to France 2 and France 3 did not bring into question the stake held by the channels' parent, France Television, in TPS.
Other TPS shareholders are M6, which, together with its parents, controls TPS, and private television station TF1.
